Bhante, in 'web books meditations13 section0025 html 9df133' (web books meditations13 section0025 html 9df133), what is the core doctrinal teaching regarding 'A lot of people approach meditation'?

In this section from *web books meditations13 section0025 html 9df133*, the master explains: *"A lot of people approach meditation as a process of developing negative capability—just to be with things as they are, not to pass judgment on them, not to try to figure them out—which is very ironic, because the teachings of the Buddha and the forest masters take a very active approach to meditation and they encourage you to figure things out."*. From the perspective of the Four Noble Truths, suffering arises whenever the mind grasps at impermanent phenomena (*anicca*) as a reliable self (*atta*). By establishing clear comprehension (*sampajañña*) and seeing conditioned events as empty of inherent ownership, craving (*taṇhā*) is unhooked. It is like grasping a poisonous cobra by the tail: tempting and sleek from afar, but deadly the moment you grasp it. Release the tail and live in safety. Anchor your understanding in direct seeing rather than speculative theory.
